verdict.rationale: Unity documents public scripting APIs and editor-extension APIs in its first-party manual, which is the base this story depends on. However, nothing in the pack speaks to API stability over time, the volume of public code examples, or how reliably LLM-generated Unity code works on the first try. Machine-readable docs are uneven: docs.unity.com serves an llms.txt, but docs.unity3d.com returns 404 for llms.txt and has no .md mirrors. Missing for 10: evidence of API stability/backward compatibility, evidence of abundant public examples, hands-on or independent reports of first-try LLM code success, machine-readable scripting API reference.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, LLM-generated code mostly works on the first try — stable, well-documented APIs with abundant public examples the models have seen

citations.quote: Interacting directly with the public Unity APIs allows for finer control and a greater degree of customization.
Unity lets you extend the editor with your own custom inspectors and Editor Windows and you can define how properties are displayed in the inspector with custom Property Drawers
docs.unity.com also serves a site-wide llms.txt index ('# Unity Documentation')
